messages:
emily: Heads-up — seeing duplicate POSTs from a sample app using the py async client after a transient 502 + connection reset. Looks like the client replays the queued request body even for non-idempotent endpoints.

sam: ugh, do you have logs? :eyes:

emily: logs attached inline. TL;DR: upstream 502, then TCP reset. SDK backoff queued the request and replayed body. got two resources created with different ids.

emily: log snippet:
```
2026-02-12T15:21:14Z INFO outgoing POST /v1/resources 502
2026-02-12T15:21:14Z ERROR connection reset by peer during request body send
2026-02-12T15:21:15Z INFO retry queued (attempt=1) backoff=250ms
2026-02-12T15:21:15Z INFO retry sending queued request
2026-02-12T15:21:15Z INFO 201 Created resource id=rec_01A
```
```
2026-02-12T15:21:16Z INFO retry finished (attempt=1) but original request apparently also succeeded upstream -> duplicate create detected: rec_01A and rec_01B
```

emily: sample app snippet (simplified):
```
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], timeout=10)
await client.post('/v1/resources', json={"name": "demo"})
```

emily: we didn't set an Idempotency-Key in the sample app because it's a quick PoC.

ritika: that's rough. Do we replay bodies by default for async client? I thought we only queue simple idempotent ops.

andrew: SDK currently stores the request payload in-memory for retries for convenience. For streaming bodies we mark non-replayable, but multipart/json bodies are replayable. The bug is the queued retry isn't checking whether the original TCP write may have succeeded before replaying.

sam: so race: server accepted but connection tear -> client assumed failure and replayed -> double create.

emily: exactly. Customer-facing sample app hit this during a demo, pretty bad.

andrew: short-term workaround: set explicit Idempotency-Key header for mutating endpoints in sample apps. Also increase timeout so we avoid early replay in flaky infra.

ritika: can we detect partial writes on the socket and avoid replaying unless we get a clean failure before headers are sent?

andrew: we need to surface a safe default: make non-idempotent POSTs non-replayable unless user sets Idempotency-Key or opt-in. Breaking change though.

emily: proposal: default SDK behavior change: mark POST without "Idempotency-Key" as non-replayable. Add a verbose warning in dev mode if retry attempted.

sam: +1 to safer default. Also add a devx guide in samples that clearly shows adding Idempotency-Key for create endpoints.

andrew: I'll open an issue and a small PR for the runtime guard and a new telemetry counter (replay_blocked_non_idempotent).

andrew: issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/412 (WIP)

ci-bot: build queued for PR #842 (sdk-python) :github:

ritika: can we add an integration test that simulates a 502 then reset and asserts no duplicate create when no idempotency key?

andrew: yes — will add a flaky-server test harness hitting the async client with connection reset mid-send.

emily: action items:
- andrew: PR for default non-replayable POSTs + telemetry (ETA 2d)
- andrew: add integration test in CI (ETA 3d)
- sam: update sample apps to include Idempotency-Key examples (ETA 1d)
- ritika: add doc blurb in SDK quickstart about idempotency and retries (ETA 1d)

sam: thanks, folks. If anyone else sees duplicates from demo apps ping here. :thumbsup:

emily: filing a support note for the customer who hit this. will CC eng on the support ticket.

andrew: follow-up: thinking about an opt-in flag client.replay_policy = 'safe'|'aggressive' so users can choose. but default should be safe.

ritika: makes sense. also add a lint rule in sampleapp CI to fail if POST sample code lacks Idempotency-Key example.

emily: nice. closing the loop after the PR lands.

ci-bot: PR #842 passed unit tests, integration pending.
